slides.title: Working with Python's `threading` Module
slides.prompt: The `threading` module provides lightweight execution threads. Threads share memory space within a process. You start execution with `start()` and wait for completion using `join()`.
slides.codeSnippet:
import threading
import time

def worker(name):
    print(f"Thread {name}: starting")
    time.sleep(1)
    print(f"Thread {name}: finishing")

t1 = threading.Thread(target=worker, args=("A",))
t1.start()
t1.join()  # Wait for t1 to complete
print("Main thread done")

slides.title: Purpose of thread.join()
slides.prompt: What does invoking `thread.join()` do in the calling thread?
options: Blocks execution until the target thread terminates
Merges two running threads into a single process
Forcefully terminates the child thread immediately
Pauses thread execution until a lock is released
slides.correctAnswer: Blocks execution until the target thread terminates

slides.title: Daemon Threads Behavior
slides.prompt: How do daemon threads behave when the main Python program exits?
options: Daemon threads are abruptly terminated when non-daemon threads exit
Daemon threads prevent the main program from exiting until finished
Daemon threads raise an UnhandledThreadException and restart
Daemon threads automatically convert into separate processes
slides.correctAnswer: Daemon threads are abruptly terminated when non-daemon threads exit
